_meta.indication: IMPAVIDO (miltefosine) is indicated in adults and adolescents >=12 years of age weighing >=30 kg for treatment of visceral leishmaniasis due to Leishmania donovani; cutaneous leishmaniasis due to Leishmania braziliensis, Leishmania guyanensis, and Leishmania panamensis; and mucosal leishmaniasis due to Leishmania braziliensis.

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, open-label, active-controlled non-inferiority trial comparing oral miltefosine with intravenous amphotericin B (15 mg/kg total, every other day over 30 days); subjects randomized 3:1.
pivotal_trials.population: Subjects >=12 years of age with signs and symptoms compatible with visceral leishmaniasis parasitologically confirmed by spleen aspirate.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary efficacy endpoint was Final Cure (at 6 months).
pivotal_trials.result: Final cure (sponsor ITT) 94.3% miltefosine vs 97.0% amphotericin B; difference 2.7% (95% CI -1.62%, 6.93%), demonstrating non-inferiority. FDA ITT analysis: 90.3% vs 94.9%; difference 4.6% (95% CI -2.0, 9.8).

pivotal_trials.phase: Not stated (no trial phase number is given for Study 3168 in the review).
pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial in Colombia and Guatemala; patients randomized 2:1 to miltefosine 50 mg or matching placebo.
pivotal_trials.population: Subjects >=12 years of age with parasitologically confirmed cutaneous leishmaniasis lesions and without underlying medical conditions or laboratory abnormalities.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary endpoint was apparent or partial cure at 2 weeks followed by definite cure at 6 months.
pivotal_trials.result: Miltefosine superior to placebo for definite cure: 66% (59/89) vs 30% (13/44); treatment difference 36.8% (95% CI 20.1%, 53.4%); p<0.0001.

key_safety: Adverse reactions occurring in >=20% of patients include nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, headache, decreased appetite, dizziness, abdominal pain, pruritus, somnolence, elevated transaminases, and elevated creatinine. In the VL trial, vomiting occurred in 37.8% (vs 20.0%) and diarrhea in 20.4% (vs 6.1%); serious adverse reactions in 2% (6/299) and <1% died (2/299).
target_moa: Miltefosine is an alkyllysophospholipid analogue with in vitro activity against Leishmania species; once internalized it inhibits mitochondrial function via inhibition of cytochrome C oxidase and inhibits phospholipid and sterol synthesis via inhibition of phospholipase C, resulting in apoptotic-like cell death.
modality: Small molecule (orally administered alkyllysophospholipid analogue, hexadecylphosphocholine).

boxed_warning.content: WARNING: EMBRYO-FETAL TOXICITY — IMPAVIDO may cause fetal harm; fetal death and teratogenicity occurred in animals at doses lower than the recommended human dose. Do not administer to pregnant women; obtain a serum or urine pregnancy test prior to prescribing and advise effective contraception during and after therapy.

advisory_committee.vote: The Advisory Committee met on October 18, 2013 and recommended approval of miltefosine for VL (15-1 vote), CL (14-2 vote), and ML (13-3 vote).

orphan_indication.text: Miltefosine was granted orphan designation on October 10, 2006 (and is therefore exempt from PREA).

summary.text: Miltefosine (Impavido) received orphan drug designation (October 10, 2006) and priority review for the treatment of visceral, cutaneous, and mucosal leishmaniasis; the drug is a new molecular entity submitted under 505(b)(1) and was eligible for the Tropical Diseases Priority Review Voucher. The original NDA received a Refuse to File letter in November 2012; the resubmission was reviewed with an advisory committee (October 18, 2013) and approved in 2014.

citations.quote: Miltefosine was granted orphan designation on October 10, 2006.
The recommendation is to grant NDA 204684 priority review.

If priority review is granted, NDA 204684 would be eligible and recommended to receive the Tropical Diseases Priority Review Voucher. Miltefosine is intended for the treatment of a listed tropical disease, is submitted under section 505(b)1 of the FD&C act and is a new molecular entity.
A Refuse to File letter was communicated to the sponsor on November 26, 2012.
The Advisory Committee met on October 18, 2013. The recommendations were to:

requirement.text: 2127-1: Collect and analyze data regarding pregnancy outcomes for 10 years after approval in women who become pregnant while taking Impavido or during 5 months after end of therapy.

citations.quote: ## **2127-1** Collect and analyze data regarding pregnancy outcomes for 10 years after approval of Impavido (miltefosine) in women who become pregnant while taking Impavido (miltefosine) or during 5 months after end of Impavido (miltefosine) therapy.

requirement.text: 2127-2: Conduct a study to evaluate the effects of Impavido on spermatogenesis and male hormones in patients with leishmaniasis receiving treatment (semen volume, sperm count, concentration, motility, total testosterone, FSH).

citations.quote: ## **2127-2** Conduct a study to evaluate the effects of Impavido (miltefosine) on spermatogenesis and male hormones in patients with leishmaniasis receiving Impavido (miltefosine) treatment. Evaluations will include semen volume, sperm count, sperm concentration and motility as well as evaluation of total testosterone and FSH.

requirement.text: 2127-3: Conduct a dedicated QT study in leishmaniasis patients receiving Impavido treatment to evaluate the effects on the QT interval.

citations.quote: ## **2127-3** Conduct a dedicated QT study in leishmaniasis patients receiving Impavido (miltefosine) treatment to evaluate the effects of Impavido (miltefosine) on the QT interval. ECGs and PK samples will be obtained to identify potential effects of Impavido (miltefosine) on the QT interval or other ECG parameters.

requirement.text: 2127-4: Conduct a descriptive study regarding efficacy outcome and adverse reactions in patients with leishmaniasis who weigh more than 75 kg.
